prompt: Daily returns of a small-cap index show significant autocorrelation at lag 1.
why: Model the mean (e.g. AR(1)) before or jointly with GARCH.
trap: Autocorrelation in returns themselves is a mean problem.

prompt: You fit an AR(1) mean and a GARCH(1,1) variance in one maximum-likelihood estimation.
tells: AR(1) mean and a GARCH(1,1) variance in one
why: ARMA-GARCH estimates mean and variance together.
trap: GARCH-M puts σ in the mean; AR puts lagged returns.

prompt: Returns are systematically lower on Mondays, which inflates the GARCH residuals.
why: Add a calendar dummy to the mean equation.
trap: The mean equation is where predictable return patterns go.

prompt: A beginner feeds raw prices instead of returns into a GARCH model.
why: Model returns (log differences) with an appropriate mean; prices are non-stationary.
trap: Getting the mean input right comes first.

prompt: After fitting GARCH(1,1) with a constant mean, Ljung–Box on standardized residuals (not squared) is significant.
why: Leftover autocorrelation in levels points to the mean model.
trap: Squared would point to variance; this is levels.

prompt: Oil returns depend on yesterday's inventory surprise, and you want that in the model alongside time-varying volatility.
why: Exogenous regressors belong in the mean equation, with GARCH on the residuals.
trap: It's a predictor of returns, not of variance.
